instruction: Shell Model With Construction Sequence Use the opened Bonsai IFC authoring environment to create a new metric IFC4 shell model with a construction task sequence and a matching CSV schedule. Save the outputs as /home/user/Desktop/result.ifc and /home/user/Desktop/result.csv. The IFC must contain one project, one site, one building, and one storey named Level 00; four walls; one slab; one door; one opening; one void relationship; one fill relationship; one IfcWorkSchedule; four IfcTask entities; and three IfcRelSequence relationships. Do not include spaces, windows, proxies, furniture, roofs, columns, beams, stairs, or flow terminals, and keep every IfcRoot GlobalId unique. Name the slab Shell Slab and make it 4.00 m by 3.00 m by 0.20 m. Model each wall 3.00 m high and 0.20 m thick. Name the door Shell Door, give it OverallWidth 0.90 m, and make it fill one opening that voids a wall. Assign the walls, slab, and door to Level 00. Name the work schedule Shell Sequence. Create tasks named Cast Slab, Build Walls, Install Door, and QC Handover with ISO durations P2D, P4D, P1D, and P1D. Sequence them directly as Cast Slab before Build Walls, Build Walls before Install Door, and Install Door before QC Handover. The CSV must use the exact headers TaskName, DurationDays, DirectPredecessor and contain four rows in this order: Cast Slab with 2 and no predecessor, Build Walls with 4 and Cast Slab, Install Door with 1 and Build Walls, and QC Handover with 1 and Install Door. Other representation details may vary. [Software] Bonsai workflows are used together with Blender; start Blender with `blender` (adjust path if needed).
